paite: Huan Nebukadnezzar vaihawm kum nih kum in Nebukednezzar in mang a neia; a lungsim a buai mahmaha, a ihmu theita kei hi.
english: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him.

paite: Huan kumpipan mitkhialdawitawite leh, bummite leh, aisanmite leh Kaldai mite, kumpipa a mang hilh dinga sap dingin thu a piaa. Huchiin a hong lut ua kumpipa maah a hong ding ta uhi.
english: Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the enchanters, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.

paite: Huchiin kumpipan a kiang uah, Mang ka neia, mang thei dingin ka lungsim a buai mahmah hi, a chi a.
english: The king said to them, I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.

paite: Huan Kaldai miten kumpipa kiangah Suria pauin, Aw kumpia, khantawnin dam in; na sikhate mang tuh hilh inla a hilhchetna ka ensak ding uh, a chi ua.
english: Then spoke the Chaldeans to the king in the Syrian language, O king, live forever: tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.

paite: Kumpipan a dawnga, Kaldai mite kiangah, A thil keia kipan a paikheta; mang ka kianga na hontheih sak kei ua leh hilhchetna toh, at nenin na om ding ua, na inte uh ekvum a honghi ding.
english: The king answered the Chaldeans, The thing is gone from me: if you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be cut in pieces, and your houses shall be made a dunghill.

paite: Himahleh mang leh a hilhchetna na theihsak ua leh, kei a kipanin thilpiakte leh kipahmante leh nakpitaka zahtakna na mu ding uh; huaijiakin mang leh a hilhchetna hon ensak un, a chi a.
english: But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive of me gifts and rewards and great honor: therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.

paite: A nihveina dingin amau a dawng ua, Kumpipan mang tuh honhilh henla, huan kou a hilhchetna ka ensak ding uh, a chi ua.
english: They answered the second time and said, Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.

paite: Kumpipan a dawnga, Kei akipanin a thil a pai kheta chih na muh jiak un, hun lei tum na hi uh chih ka thei tel hi.
english: The king answered, I know of a certainty that you would gain time, because you see the thing is gone from me.

paite: Ahihhangin mang tuh ka kianga na kitheih sak kei u leh, nou adingin dan khat kia a om; hun a kikhen tana, ka maa thu juau leh sia gelkhol na hih jiak un; huaijiakin mang tuh honhilh unla, huan a hilhchetna na hon ensak thei uh chih ka thei ding, a chi a.
english: But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the time be changed: therefore tell me the dream, and I shall know that you can show me its interpretation.

paite: Kaldai miten kumpipa maah a dawng ua, Kumpipa thu ensak thei leitungah kumah a om kei; kumpipa hiam, toupa hiam, vaihawmmi kuamahin mitkhialdawitawi kuamahmah hiam, bummi kuamahmah hiam, Kaldai mi kuamahmah ah huchibang a dot ngei louh jiak un.
english: The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler, has asked such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Chaldean.

paite: Kumpipa thil deih vangtak ahi, pathiante a omna uh sa toh hiloute chihlouhngal, midang kuamahin kumpipa maah huai a ensak theikei ding uh, a chi ua.
english: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.

paite: Hiai jiakin kumpipa a heh mahmaha a thangpai tuntuna, Babulon mi pilte tengteng hihmang dingin thu a peta hi.
english: For this cause the king was angry and very furious, and commanded to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.

paite: Huchiin thupiak a pai khetaa, mi pilte a thah ding ahi ta ua; huan Danial leh a lawmte thah dingin a zong uhi.
english: So the decree went forth, and the wise men were to be slain; and they sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.

paite: Huchiin Danialin kumpipa veng sepaih zaheutu Ariok kiangah thuhilhna leh thupil toh dawnna a kik saka, Babulon mi pilte that dinga kuankhe pa kiangah.
english: Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who was gone forth to kill the wise men of Babylon;

paite: Ariok kumpipa sepaih zaheutu a dawnga a kiangah, Bangdia kumpipa a kipan thupiak huchitela kin ahia? a chi a. Huchiin Ariokin Danial kiangah a thil a kitheisak a.
english: he answered Arioch the king’s captain, Why is the decree so urgent from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.

paite: Huan Danial a luta, amah adia hun sehsak dingin kumpipa a ngena, huchia a hilh chetna kumpipa a etsak dingin.
english: Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.

paite: Huchiin Danial a in ah a paia, Hanania te, Misael te, Azaria te, a lawmte kiangah huai thil tuh a theisak ta hi;
english: Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions:

paite: Huchia amauten hiai thuguk tanchina van Pathian chitnate a nget theihna dingun; huchia Danial leh a lawmte Babulon a mi pilte lakate toh amanthat louhna ding un.
english: that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his companions should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

paite: Huchiin jan mengmuhna ah Danial kiangah thuguk tuh taklatin a om ta hi. Huan Danialin van Pathian a phat hi.
english: Then was the secret revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.

paite: Danialin a dawnga, Khantawn khantawnin Pathian min phatin om hen; Pilna leh hatna lah amaha ahi ngala;
english: Daniel answered, Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his.

paite: Huan aman hunte leh hunbite a hihlamdanga; kumpipate a suan khia, kumpipate a tung khiaa; mi pilte kiangah pilna a piaa, theihsiamna theite kiangah theihna a pia hi.
english: He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding;

paite: Thil thukte leh gukte a taklanga, miala om bang ahia aman a thei a, a kiangah khovak a om hi.
english: he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.

paite: Na tungah ka kipaka, ka honphat hi. Aw nang ka pipute Pathian, pilna leh hatna honpe pa, leh nang ka honnget uh tua ka kianga hontheisakpa; kumpipa thu lah ka kiang uah na hontheisak ta ngala, a chi a.
english: I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.

paite: Huaijiakin Danial, kumpipan Babulon mi pilte hihse dia a sehpa, Ariok kiangah a hoh a; a vahoha a kiangah hichibangin a chi hi; Babulon mipilte hihmang ken; kumpipa maah honpi lut inla, huan kumpipa kiangah a hilhchetna ka ensak ding, a chi a.
english: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and said thus to him: Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.

paite: Huchiin Ariokin kintakin kumpipa maah Danial a pi luta, a kiangah hichibangin a chi a; Juda saltangte lak ah mi khat ka mu a, aman kumpipa kiangah a hilhchetna a theisak ding, a chi a.
english: Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and said thus to him, I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judah, who will make known to the king the interpretation.

paite: Kumpipan a dawnga Danial kiangah, a min Beltesazar hiven, Mang ka neih na hon theisak theiin, a hilhchetna na hon theisak thei maw? a chi a.
english: The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?

paite: Danial in kumpipa maah a dawnga, Thuguk kumpipan a nget mipil hiin, aisanmite hileh, kumpipa kiangah a ensak theikei ding ua.
english: Daniel answered before the king, and said, The secret which the king has demanded can neither wise men, enchanters, magicians, nor soothsayers, show to the king;

paite: Himahleh van ah Pathian a oma aman thugukte a taklang hi; ni nanung lama bang ahia om ding kumpipa Nebukadnezzar kiangah a theisak ta hi. Na lupna tunga na lutang mengmuhna leh na mang hiaite ahi;
english: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:

paite: Nang na hih leh aw kumpipa na lupna tungah na lungsim sungah na ngeihtuahnate a hongom ua; tunung chianga bang ahia hongom ding thu: huan amah thugukte na kianga taklangpan bang ahia hongom ding na kiangah a theisak ta ahi.
english: as for you, O king, your thoughts came into your mind on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.

paite: Himahleh kei bel, pilna ahing himhim sanga pilna ka neih tam jawk jiaka hiai thuguk ka kianga taklat ahi keia: himahleh a hilhchetna kumpipa kianga theihsak a hih theihna ding leh nang na lungtang ngaihtuahte na theihna ding a hijaw hi.
english: But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.

paite: Nang, Aw kumpipa, namuta; ngaiin, milim thupi tak. Hiai milim, hat tak mai, a tetna thupi mahmah, na maah a ding a; amel tuh a kihtakhuai mahmah hi.
english: You, O king, saw, and behold, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its aspect was awesome.

paite: Hiai milim a hih leh, a lutang dangkaeng hoih ahi a. a awm leh a bante dangka, a gilleh apheipite dal,
english: As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass,

paite: akhete sik, a khepekte sikkhenkhatleh tung khenkhat.
english: its legs of iron, its feet part of iron, and part of clay.

paite: Suang khuta sek louh. huai milim a khepek sik, leh tung denga kitam nen sak dimdem tanin na mu a.
english: You saw until a stone was cut out without hands, which struck the image on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.

paite: Huchiin sik toh, tung toh. dal toh, dangka toh, dangkaeng loh a kitam nen khawm vek ua: nipi buhphuala buhsi bang mai a hong hi ua; huchiin huihin amaute amut mang ua: huan huai milim deng suang pen mual thupi a hong suaka. lei pumpi a dimta hi.
english: Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them: and the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.

paite: Hiai mang ahi a; kumpipa maah a hilhchetna ka gen ding uh.
english: This is the dream; and we will tell its interpretation before the king.

paite: Nang. Aw kumpipa, kumpipate kumpipa, van Pathianin a kianga gam te, thilhihtheihna te. hatna te, thupina te a piak. na hi a;
english: You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, and the strength, and the glory;

paite: huan koipeuha mite tate a tenna uah, gama sate leh vana vasate na khut ah a honpia; amaute tengteng tunga lal dingin nang a honbawla: dangkaeng lutang na hi.
english: and wherever the children of men dwell, the animals of the field and the birds of the sky has he given into your hand, and has made you to rule over them all: you are the head of gold.

paite: Huan nang nungin nanga sanga niamjaw gam dang khat a hong ding khe ding; huchiin lal gam thumna dang, leitung tengtenga thunei ding.
english: After you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you; and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth.

paite: Huan gam lina sik bangin a hat dinga: sikin a kek nen saka thil tengteng a nuaisiah bang takin: huan sikin hiaite tengteng a delh jan angin, a kek nen sakin, a delh jan ding hi.
english: The fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, shall it break in pieces and crush.

paite: Huan khepekte leh khezung na muhte, a khen belvelmi tung leh a khen sik a hih leh, gam hawmjak ahi dinga; himahleh a sungah sik hatna a om dinga, sik buannawi tung toh helkhawmna muh-bangtakin.
english: Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it shall be a divided kingdom; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.

paite: Huan khepek khezungte akhen sik leh akhen tung hi pen a hihleh. huchibangin gam hatna chiang nei, kitapna chiang neia hi ding hi.
english: As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.

paite: Huan sik buannawi tung toh kihel na muh pen a hihleh, mite chi toh a mau a kitok hel ding uh; himahleh a kikawi kip kei ding ua. sik tung toh a kigawm lou mah bangin.
english: Whereas you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men; but they shall not cling to one another, even as iron does not mingle with clay.

paite: Huan huai kumpipate dam laiin van Pathianin gam suksiata om ngei lou ding, a thuneihna mi dang kianga nutsiata om ngei sam lou ding, a honding khe sak dinga; himahleh hiai gam tengteng a kitam nen sak dinga, a suse vek dinga, amah bel khantawnin a ding ding hi.
english: In the days of those kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall its sovereignty be left to another people; but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.

paite: Suang mual akipan khuta sek louh hongom khiaa, sik te, dal te, tung te. dangka te leh dangkaeng te a kitam sak dimdem na muh pen a hihleh; tunung chianga bang ahia hongom ding kumpipa kiang ah Pathian thupiin a thei sakta hi: huan mang tuh theihsa ahia, a hilhchetna a kichian hi, a chi a,
english: Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what shall happen hereafter: and the dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.

paite: Huaitakin Nebukadnezzarin a maiin lei a sia, Danial a bia a. thillat leh gim namtui a kianga lan dingin amau thu a pia hi.
english: Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, and worshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odors to him.

paite: Kumpipan Danial a dawnga, Chihtaktakin na Pathian pathiante Pathian leh, kumpipate TOUPA leh, thugukte taklangpa ahi; hiai thuguk taklang dinga hihtheihna na neih jiakin, a chi a.
english: The king answered to Daniel, and said, Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.

paite: Huchiin kumpipan Danial a lian saka, thilpiak tampi a piaa. Babulon bial pumpia heutuin a bawla. Babulon mi pilte tengteng tunga ukpipa pen dingin.Huan Danial in Sadrak te, Mesak te, Abed-nego te Babulon bial thulehla tunga koih dingin kumpipa kiangah a ngena; himahleh Danial jaw kumpipa kongpi ah a om hi.
english: Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him to rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.

paite: Huan Danial in Sadrak te, Mesak te, Abed-nego te Babulon bial thulehla tunga koih dingin kumpipa kiangah a ngena; himahleh Danial jaw kumpipa kongpi ah a om hi.
english: Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon: but Daniel was in the gate of the king.
